title: Tuning and evaluating a random forest regressor

items.stem: Definitions: In a random forest regressor, what does the max_features setting control?

options.text: The number of features each tree is trained on, chosen once per tree
The number of features kept after dropping the least important ones
The number of features randomly drawn as split candidates at each split
The most distinct features a single tree may use across all its splits

items.stem: Definitions: In one phrase, what restriction does the min_samples_leaf setting place on a regression tree?
Definitions: Which of these best defines the out-of-bag (OOB) score of a random forest regressor?

options.text: Prediction error on each row, using only trees whose bootstrap sample excluded that row
Training error of each tree, averaged over the rows that tree was grown on
Error on a held-out test set that the forest never saw during fitting
Error of the whole averaged forest on the rows it was fitted on

items.stem: Definitions: Which statement about the n_estimators setting of a random forest regressor is correct?

options.text: The number of bootstrap rows drawn from the data to train each single tree
The maximum depth each tree is allowed to grow to
The minimum number of rows each leaf must keep
The size of the ensemble: how many trees are fitted before predicting

items.stem: Definitions: Which statement correctly describes the RMSE of a regression model?

options.text: The share of the target's variance that the model explains, on a scale up to 1
A typical size of the prediction errors, in the target's units, where large misses count extra
The average absolute size of the prediction errors, in the target's units, with every miss counted equally
The mean of the squared prediction errors, in the target's units squared

items.stem: Applying it: A forest of 100 trees with max_features=0.5 and min_samples_leaf=1 is fitted to 50,000 rows with the OOB score switched on. It reaches a training R² of 0.98 and an OOB R² of 0.71. Raising n_estimators to 300 left the OOB R² at 0.71, and the average pairwise correlation between the trees' predictions is 0.8. Which change is most likely to raise the OOB R²?

options.text: Raise n_estimators from 100 to 300 so the average has lower variance
Raise min_samples_leaf from 1 to 10 so each tree fits less noise
Raise max_features from 0.5 to 1.0 so every split compares all the features
Standardize every feature to mean 0 and variance 1 so the splits are better scaled

items.stem: Applying it: At one input, each of the 100 trees in a forest has prediction variance 4. The predictions of any two different trees have correlation 0.5. What is the variance of the forest's averaged prediction at that input?

Applying it: An analyst fits a forest for each of 60 combinations of settings, scores every one on the same 2,000-row test set, and reports the best test R² as the expected performance on new data. How does that figure compare with the true performance on new data?

options.text: Likely too high: that combination was picked because it scored well on these particular rows
Likely about right: the forest never trained on the test rows, so its score on them is unbiased
Likely too low: settings chosen on rows the forest never trained on are under-fitted to them
Likely about right: R² changes little between settings, so the best of 60 is close to the others

items.stem: Applying it: Two tuned forests predict house prices. On the same four validation rows, forest A has errors (predicted minus actual) of +1, -2, +2 and -4 thousand dollars, and forest B has errors of +2, -2, +2 and -2 thousand dollars. The team ranks forests by RMSE, lower being better. What is the RMSE of the forest that ranks worse, in thousand dollars?

Applying it: A soccer analytics team fits forests to predict expected goals from shot data. The OOB R² is 0.80 with 25 trees, 0.868 with 100 trees, 0.872 with 400 trees and 0.873 with 1,600 trees. Training cost grows in proportion to the number of trees. The team will give up at most 0.002 of OOB R² compared with the best forest it tried, and wants the lowest training cost. Which number of trees should it use?

options.text: 25, because training cost is the main concern and 0.80 is acceptable
100, because the curve has already flattened by that point
400, because the extra 1,200 trees would add only 0.001 of OOB R²
1,600, because it scores highest and training cost grows only in direct proportion
